title: IDEX Corporation Declares Regular Quarterly Cash Dividend
content:
NORTHBROOK, Ill., May 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--IDEX CORPORATION (NYSE:IEX) today announced that its Board of Directors has approved a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.73 per common share. This dividend will be paid June 5, 2026 to shareholders of record as of May 22, 2026. This dividend represents the company’s 126th consecutive regular quarterly cash dividend payment.

About IDEX

IDEX Corporation (NYSE: IEX), a global engineered products company, is comprised of three primary business segments – Health & Science Technologies, Fluid & Metering Technologies, and Fire & Safety / Diversified Products. Thousands of IDEX employees around the world design and manufacture highly engineered components and applied solutions that are vital to the advances of modern life and help IDEX live its purpose – Trusted Solutions, Improving Lives™. From satellite communications to water systems, from medical diagnostic components to emergency rescue tools and more, we collaborate with customers in the most critical industries to develop solutions that make the world better today and into the future. Founded in 1988, IDEX now includes more than 50 dynamic businesses around the world and manufacturing operations in more than 20 countries. Learn more about the impactful work we do at www.idexcorp.com.

title: IDEX Beats Q1 Earnings Estimates on HST Momentum, Raises View
content:
IDEX Corporation IEX delivered first-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $2.00 per share, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.78 by 12.4%. The metric rose 14.3% year over year. Net sales of $886.9 million beat the consensus mark of $835 million by 6.2% and increased 8.9% from the year-ago quarter.

Results were driven by solid traction in the Health & Science Technologies segment, where higher volumes in AI-linked data center power and semiconductor end markets, along with strength in space and defense, supported growth. IDEX also posted record orders, signaling improving demand early in 2026.

Organic sales increased 5% year over year. While acquisitions/divestitures had a positive impact on sales of 1%, foreign currency translation had a positive impact of 3% on sales.

IDEX Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS SurpriseIDEX Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

IDEX Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | IDEX Corporation Quote

Segmental Details

Net sales from the Fluid & Metering Technologies segment totaled $301.5 million, up 4% year over year. Our estimate for segmental net sales was $297.3 million. Organic sales increased 2% year over year. Foreign currency translation had a positive impact of 2% on sales.

Net sales from the Health & Science Technologies segment totaled $398.4 million, up 17% year over year. Organic sales increased 11% year over year. Acquisitions/divestitures and foreign currency translation had a positive impact of 3% each on sales.

Net sales from the Fire & Safety/Diversified Products segment totaled $188.3 million, which increased 2% year over year. Our estimate for segmental net sales was $182 million. Organic sales decreased 1% on a year-over-year basis, while foreign currency translation had a favorable impact of 3% on sales.

IEX’s Orders Signal Broad-Based Demand

Orders increased 13% year over year to $988.3 million, with organic orders up 10%. Management pointed to momentum and backlog building in businesses tied to several end markets, particularly AI-driven areas, pharma and space and defense.

IDEX’s Margin Profile

IDEX’s cost of sales increased 9.7% year over year to $488.8 million. The adjusted gross margin was 44.9%, down 40 basis points year over year, reflecting unfavorable mix and higher costs, partially offset by productivity improvements and volume leverage. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased to $218.3 million from $209.4 million in the prior-year period.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 10.8% to $230.4 million and the adjusted EBITDA margin improved 50 basis points to 26%. Operating income increased 21.4% to $172.4 million, aided by stronger operating performance and a lower restructuring and asset impairment burden compared to the prior year period. The operating margin was 19.4%, up 200 bps year over year. Interest expenses (net) were relatively stable year over year at $16 million.

Story Continues

IEX’s Cash Uses Highlight Shareholder Returns

Cash flows from operating activities were $103.7 million compared with $105.7 million a year ago, as increased earnings were offset by customer payment timing. Free cash flow declined 5.9% to $86 million, reflecting both working-capital timing and higher capital expenditures of $17.7 million.

The company continued to return capital, repurchasing $76.3 million of stock and paying $52.8 million in dividends during the quarter. On the balance sheet, cash and cash equivalents were $586.2 million exiting the first quarter, while long-term borrowings (net) stood at $1.87 billion.

IDEX’s Raised 2026 Outlook Reflects Confidence

Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, projecting organic sales growth of 3-4% compared with prior expectations of 1-2%. The company also lifted its full-year adjusted earnings outlook to $8.35-$8.55 per share from $8.15-$8.35 previously.

For the second quarter of 2026, IDEX expects organic sales to increase 3-4% from the year-ago period and expects adjusted earnings in the range of $2.07-$2.12.

The company currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell). Some better-ranked stocks are discussed below:

DXP Enterprises DXPE presently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

DXP Enterprises’ earnings surpassed the consensus estimate by 52.8% in the last reported quarter. In the past 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for DXPE’s 2026 earnings has increased by 17.2%.

Nordson Corporation NDSN currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Nordson’s earnings topped the consensus estimate in each of the trailing four quarters. The average earnings surprise was 2.5%. In the past 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for Nordson’s fiscal 2026 earnings has increased 0.5%.

RBC Bearings RBC presently carries a Zacks Rank of 2. RBC Bearings’ earnings surpassed the consensus estimate in each of the trailing four quarters. The average earnings surprise was 5.3%. title: IDEX Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
content:
IDEX logo

Industrial Tech Crossovers: When Manufacturing Meets Innovation

IDEX (NYSE:IEX) reported first-quarter 2026 results that management said came in above expectations, supported by growth in its targeted “advantage markets” and continued application of the company’s 80/20 operating philosophy.

Quarterly performance and orders

President and CEO Eric Ashleman said IDEX delivered 5% organic sales growth in the quarter and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 26%, representing 50 basis points of year-over-year margin expansion. He also highlighted that orders were “better than expected,” with organic orders up 10% year-over-year.

→ Palantir Is Down 30%: Noise? Or a Signal to Accumulate?

Chief Financial Officer Sean Gillen said the quarter benefited from strength in Health & Science Technologies (HST), while the company also saw improved trends in parts of its shorter-cycle industrial exposure. “Adjusted EPS came in significantly higher than our guided range in the first quarter,” Gillen said, though he did not provide the specific Q1 adjusted EPS figure during the call.

On profitability, Gillen said adjusted EBITDA margin expansion was driven by “productivity improvements, positive volume leverage, and positive price cost,” partially offset by mix. Adjusted gross margin declined 40 basis points year-over-year to 44.9%, which he attributed to productivity gains and volume leverage being “more than offset by mix.”

Segment results: HST backlog builds while short-cycle markets remain mixed

→ Corning Beats Q1 Estimates but Drops 9% on Guidance Miss

Management repeatedly pointed to HST as the key driver of the quarter. Ashleman said strength was “most pronounced” in HST, citing secular drivers in data center, semiconductor, and space and defense markets, and noted that backlog building in HST improved visibility “for the balance of the year and into 2027.”

HST: Gillen said organic orders increased 17% and organic revenue grew 11%. He cited volume gains in semiconductor original equipment and consumables, data center applications, and space and defense, and also called out strength in pharma. HST adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 basis points year-over-year. Fluid & Metering Technologies (FMT): Gillen said organic orders increased 9% and organic sales increased 2%. Orders were helped by IDEX’s “intelligent water platform” and mining exposure, partially offset by “global softness in chemical end markets.” FMT adjusted EBITDA margin declined 10 basis points year-over-year due to mix and volume deleverage outweighing productivity benefits. Fire & Safety/Diversified Products (FSDP): Gillen said organic orders declined 4% and organic sales decreased 1%. Fire & Safety grew “high single digit,” driven by strong demand for fire and rescue tools in North America and stable demand in Europe, offset by an expected decline in dispensing tied to difficult project comparisons. FSDP adjusted EBITDA margin increased 30 basis points year-over-year on productivity improvements.

Story Continues

On the cadence of short-cycle demand, Ashleman described January as soft, February improved, and March “much stronger,” with April holding around March levels. Still, he said the company’s internal “diagnostic” businesses were not moving “in a uniform way,” which he tied to continued geopolitical overhang and customer caution.

Advantage markets focus: space & defense, data center and semiconductors

→ Did Qualcomm Just Put Apple in Check?

Ashleman framed space and defense as an example of where IDEX is deploying resources to expand its opportunity set, describing the company’s role providing “critical components that move, manage, filter, focus, and protect data, energy, and fluids in space and defense systems.” He emphasized long program lives and rising system complexity as factors supporting a “multiyear growth runway.”

Management also discussed areas “influenced by AI,” which Gillen said were most meaningful for IDEX in power generation for data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, and optical switching. In response to analyst questions, Ashleman referenced IDEX’s thermal management role in behind-the-meter power generation used to support data centers.

Ashleman and Gillen also discussed HST profitability dynamics. Gillen said getting HST margins back toward historical highs would require improvement in acquired businesses whose margins are “not quite at the segment average yet,” plus a more favorable mix from life sciences. He said the company expects HST flow-through to improve into the mid-30% range in 2026 and sees a path “towards that 40%” as 80/20 actions take hold and as end markets improve.

On life sciences, Ashleman said the business performed “about exactly where we thought it would be,” with core franchises growing low single digits. He cited strength in pharma but pressure from China market dynamics for end customers and from NIH funding and academic pressures.

Capital deployment, cash flow, and balance sheet

IDEX generated $86 million of free cash flow in the first quarter, which Gillen described as the company’s seasonally lowest cash flow period. Free cash flow was down $5 million year-over-year, driven “mostly by higher working capital investment due to higher growth.” Gillen reiterated IDEX’s expectation of at least 100% free cash flow conversion on an annual basis.

The company ended the quarter with approximately $1.1 billion of liquidity and gross leverage of roughly two times. IDEX also continued returning capital to shareholders, paying $53 million in dividends and repurchasing $76 million of shares in the quarter. Ashleman said the company expects to maintain that repurchase pace throughout 2026, and Gillen added that IDEX still has capacity to pursue bolt-on M&A alongside its buyback plans.

Guidance raised; tariff update

Based on first-quarter performance and backlog building, IDEX raised its full-year outlook. Gillen said the company now expects 2026 organic growth of 3% to 4%, up from its prior 1% to 2% guidance. The company’s segment-level outlook assumes “high single-digit growth for HST” and “flattish” expectations for FMT and FSDP.

IDEX maintained its adjusted EBITDA margin outlook of 26.5% to 27% for the year. However, it increased its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance by $0.20 to $8.35 to $8.55. For the second quarter, Gillen guided to 3% to 4% organic growth, 26.5% to 27% adjusted EBITDA margin, and $2.07 to $2.12 adjusted EPS.

On tariffs, Gillen said the company continues to monitor developments and adapt. He noted that IEEPA tariffs have been repealed, but new tariffs have been implemented that are “largely consistent” with those repealed, leading IDEX to not anticipate “much of a net impact” to financial results at present. He added that the company has applied for expected IEEPA refunds and will update investors as the process plays out.

In closing remarks, Ashleman said HST continues to build momentum in targeted advantage markets, with wins that have “long multi-year tails,” while FMT and FSDP showed “encouraging positive signs of early inflection” but still face uncertainty tied to geopolitical factors.

About IDEX (NYSE:IEX)

IDEX Corporation is a diversified industrial manufacturer specializing in the design, production and distribution of highly engineered fluidics systems, measurement technologies and safety solutions. The company's core offerings include positive-displacement pumps, flow meters, valves, sampling systems and analytical instruments that serve a wide range of end markets such as water treatment, chemical processing, energy, food and beverage, and life sciences. Through its focus on precision engineering and proprietary material science, IDEX delivers products designed for reliability in demanding applications.

Operations at IDEX are organized into three principal segments.

title: IDEX Corporation Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
IDEX Corporation Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance Drivers

Performance was driven by a strategic pivot toward durable, high-growth markets including semiconductor, data center, and space and defense, which fueled 10% organic order growth. The Health & Science Technologies (HST) segment outperformed expectations due to secular demand for complex components that manage data, energy, and fluids in mission-critical environments. Management is increasingly utilizing 80/20 as a growth tool, deliberately segmenting markets to reallocate capital and talent toward the highest-value opportunities with winning customers. Fluid & Metering Technologies (FMT) saw strength in municipal water and mining, though results were partially offset by global softness in chemical end markets. The company is achieving a 'flywheel effect' where strengthening advantaged platforms allows for further portfolio rationalization, driving higher growth and stronger margins over time. Operational execution and productivity gains successfully offset negative mix and volume deleverage in the FMT and FSDP segments during the quarter.

Outlook and Strategic Assumptions

Full-year 2026 organic growth guidance was raised to 3-4%, assuming high single-digit growth in HST and flattish performance in FMT and FSDP. The strong backlog build in HST provides enhanced visibility into late 2026 and 2027, particularly for long-cycle space and defense programs. Management maintains a cautious outlook for general industrial markets, modeling them as flattish due to ongoing geopolitical uncertainty and mixed signals from short-cycle diagnostic businesses. Capital allocation will remain balanced, with a commitment to $76 million in quarterly share repurchases throughout 2026. alongside active pursuit of bolt-on M&A. Free cash flow conversion is expected to be at least 100% for the full year, despite higher working capital requirements to support accelerated growth.

Operational Context and Risks

Recent acquisitions like Muon, Micro-LAM, and Mott are currently dilutive to segment margins, but management expects 80/20 actions to drive them toward the segment average. The repeal of IEEPA tariffs and implementation of new administration tariffs are expected to be net-neutral to financial results. Life sciences remains a headwind due to inventory guarding by customers and funding pressures in academic and NIH-related markets. Gross margin declined 40 basis points year-over-year, primarily reflecting unfavorable product mix that offset productivity and volume gains.

Q&A Session Highlights

Path to returning HST margins to historical 30% levels

Management noted that recently acquired businesses are currently performing below the segment average, creating a margin drag despite strong growth. Improvement will depend on applying 80/20 to prune lower-margin parts of acquired portfolios and a recovery in the highly profitable life sciences business.

Sustainability of short-cycle industrial market recovery

Order cadence improved monthly from a weak January to a strong March, with stability continuing into April. Management remains guarded because diagnostic businesses are not yet moving positively in a uniform way, suggesting a mixed recovery rather than a broad inflection.

Strategic rationale for increased capital expenditure

The step-up in CapEx is specifically directed toward supporting growth in HST, including equipment for semiconductor and space applications. Management uses 80/20 to repurpose capital from declining legacy areas to fund these high-growth initiatives, keeping overall capital intensity relatively low.

Visibility and duration of the space and defense runway

Customers are providing longer-term visibility than typical for IDEX to ensure capacity and material availability for aggressive ramp-ups. The 'moat' in these markets is built through early incumbency and trusted partner status, which leads to multi-year program tails.

title: Stocks Pressured as Soaring Crude Prices Raise Inflation Concerns
content:
The S&P 500 Index ($SPX) (SPY) today is down -0.19%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DOWI) (DIA) is down -0.57%, and the Nasdaq 100 Index ($IUXX) (QQQ) is up +0.20%.  June E-mini S&P futures (ESM26) are down -0.15%, and June E-mini Nasdaq futures (NQM26) are up +0.21%.

Stock indexes are mixed today.  Soaring crude oil prices are lifting inflation expectations and bond yields and are negative for stocks.  WTI crude oil climbed to a 2-week high today after the US signaled it will maintain its naval blockade of Iran for the foreseeable future.  The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump told his aides to prepare for an extended blockade and that it carries less of a risk for the US than resuming hostilities or walking away from the conflict without securing a deal that curbs Iran’s nuclear activities.  The 10-year T-note yield is up +5 bp to a 4-week high of 4.40%.Join 200K+ Subscribers: Find out why the midday Barchart Brief newsletter is a must-read for thousands daily.

The Nasdaq 100 is higher today as technology stocks climb on signs that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong.  NXP Semiconductors NV and Seagate Technology Holdings Plc are up more than +10% to lead chipmakers and AI infrastructure stocks higher after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings results. The markets are awaiting earnings from four of the Magnificent Seven technology stocks after the close today, as Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta Platforms will report quarterly results.

Today’s US housing starts and core capital goods new orders reports were better than expected, a supportive factor for stocks.

US MBA mortgage applications fell -1.6% in the week ended April 24, with the purchase mortgage sub-index up +1.2% and the refinancing sub-index down -4.4%.  The average 30-year fixed rate mortgage rose by +2 bp to 6.37% from 6.35% in the prior week.

US Mar housing starts unexpectedly rose +10.8% m/m to a 15-month high of 1.502 million, stronger than expectations of a decline to 1.380 million. Mar building permits, a proxy for future construction, fell -10.8% m/m to a 7-month low of 1.372 million, weaker than expectations of 1.390 million.

US Mar capital goods new orders nondefense ex-aircraft and parts, a proxy for capital spending, rose +3.3% m/m, stronger than expectations of +0.5% m/m and the largest increase in 5.75 years.

WTI crude oil prices (CLM26) are up by more than +4% today as the US and Iran are locked in a battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz, with both sides blocking the waterway to gain leverage during an extended ceasefire.  The Strait of Hormuz remains essentially closed, threatening to deepen the global energy crisis, as flows of crude, natural gas, and oil products from the Persian Gulf have been cut off since the war began in late February.  The ongoing blockade could exacerbate global oil and fuel shortages, as about a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas transits through the strait.  Goldman Sachs estimates that crude output in the Persian Gulf has been curtailed by about 14.5 million bpd, or more than 50%, so far in April, and that the current disruption has drawn down nearly 500 million bbl from global crude stockpiles, which could hit a billion bbl by June.

The 2-day FOMC meeting concludes this afternoon, and the Fed is expected to keep monetary policy unchanged.  The markets will look to Fed Chair Powell's post-meeting comments for guidance on the future direction of Fed policy.  Today’s FOMC meeting is the last for Mr. Powell as Fed Chair, as his term expires on May 15.

Kevin Warsh now appears to be on a glide path toward Senate approval as the new Fed Chair after Senator Thom Tillis said on Sunday that he dropped his opposition to the nomination.  Mr. Tillis dropped his opposition after the US Justice Department dropped its criminal investigation into the Fed’s overspending on the renovation of its building, in line with Mr. Tillis’ demand.  Mr. Tillis views the investigation into Fed Chair Powell as an attempt to force the Fed to cut interest rates.  The Senate Banking Committee is due to vote on Mr. Warsh’s appointment today and then send the nomination to the full Senate for a vote.

The markets are discounting a 0% chance for a +25 bp FOMC rate hike at the Tue-Wed policy meeting.  The markets are expecting the FOMC to leave policy unchanged this week as it awaits further developments in oil prices and inflation.

Earnings season ramps up this week with several Magnificent Seven technology stocks reporting.  Earnings results thus far have been supportive of stocks.  As of today, 80% of the 199 S&P 500 companies that reported Q1 earnings have beaten estimates.  Q1 S&P 500 earnings are projected to climb +12% y/y, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.  Stripping out the technology sector, Q1 earnings are projected to increase around +3%, the weakest in two years.
